premises.statement: Every retained transaction-period rate match also has a matching reporting-period exchange-rate row for the same account and source subsidiary.
premises.alternative: The contract requires two rate joins and states: "Both joins are required; rows missing either rate are excluded."
premises.reason: Without the omitted reporting-period join, lines lacking required reporting rates remain in the result.

premises.statement: The reporting-period exchange rate equals the transaction-period exchange rate for every retained line and reporting period.
premises.alternative: The contract requires the reporting rate to match on "reporting_accounting_period_id" and the transaction rate to match on "transaction_accounting_period_id".
premises.reason: Reusing the transaction rate changes reporting-month conversions whenever rates differ between periods.

premises.statement: The period and exchange-rate joins produce at most one output row for each transaction_line_id.
premises.alternative: The output contract specifies "One row per transaction_line_id", while the period mapping permits multiple reporting periods and the exchange-rate map includes to_subsidiary_id in its grain.
premises.reason: Multiple reporting periods or target subsidiaries can violate the required unique output grain even when source keys are unique.

premises.statement: Every non-null selected legacy exchange-rate string is parseable as DOUBLE.
premises.reason: Unparseable non-null rates silently yield NULL converted amounts without an established handling rule.

premises.statement: Comparing full-precision multiplier timestamps to the current time selects the same periods as first truncating those timestamps to seconds.
premises.alternative: The contract requires "the multiplier's starting_at, truncated to seconds and interpreted as a timestamp" to be no later than the current time.
premises.reason: A fractional-second timestamp near the evaluation boundary can be excluded despite qualifying after the required truncation.
